In mathematics, the '''Teichmüller–Tukey lemma''' (sometimes named just '''Tukey's lemma'''), named after [[John Tukey]] and [[Oswald Teichmüller]], is a [[Lemma (mathematics)|lemma]] that states that every nonempty collection of [[finite character]] has a [[maximal element]] with respect to [[inclusion (set theory)|inclusion]]. Over [[Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory]], the Teichmüller–Tukey lemma is equivalent to the [[axiom of choice]], and therefore to the [[well-ordering theorem]], [[Zorn's lemma]], and the [[Hausdorff maximal principle]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Jech |first=Thomas J.|author-link=Thomas Jech |title=The Axiom of Choice |isbn=978-0-486-46624-8 |publisher=[[Dover Publications]] |year=2008 |orig-year=1973 }}</ref>

==Definitions==
A family of sets <math>\mathcal{F}</math> is of '''finite character''' provided it has the following properties:
#For each <math>A\in \mathcal{F}</math>, every [[finite set|finite]] [[subset]] of <math>A</math> belongs to  <math>\mathcal{F}</math>.
#If every finite subset of a given set <math>A</math> belongs to  <math>\mathcal{F}</math>, then <math>A</math> belongs to  <math>\mathcal{F}</math>.

==Statement of the lemma==
Let <math>Z</math> be a set and let <math>\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(Z)</math>. If <math>\mathcal{F}</math> is of finite character and <math>X\in\mathcal{F}</math>, then there is a maximal <math>Y\in\mathcal{F}</math> (according to the inclusion relation) such that <math>X\subseteq Y</math>.<ref>{{cite book |last=Kunen |first=Kenneth|title=The Foundations of Mathematics |isbn=978-1-904987-14-7 |publisher=[[College Publications]] |year=2009 }}</ref>

==Applications==
In [[linear algebra]], the lemma may be used to show the existence of a [[basis (linear algebra)|basis]]. Let ''V'' be a [[vector space]]. Consider the collection  <math>\mathcal{F}</math> of [[linearly independent]] sets of vectors. This is a collection of [[finite character]]. Thus, a maximal set exists, which must then [[span (linear algebra)|span]] ''V'' and be a basis for ''V''.
